questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Straight Line
questions.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(3,-5,-2)$ and is perpendicular to the line 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-3t \\ y=3+4t \\ z=4-t.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨3,-5,-2⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-3t \\ y=3+4t \\ z=4-t\end{aligned}\,⟹\,⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨2,3,4⟩+t\text{ }{{⟨-3,4,-1⟩}_{⏟}}_{v}.
$$

 

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨-3,4,-1⟩,$ so a normal vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨-3,4,-1⟩.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-3,4,-1⟩ & =⟨3,-5,-2⟩\cdot ⟨-3,4,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-3,4,-1⟩ & =-27.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector That Is Parallel To a Plane
questions.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩=7.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩=7$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-3,1,-2⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩ & =0 \\ -3{t}_{1}+{t}_{2}-2{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{2} & =3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{3},\,{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the first component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{1}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{3}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{3}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{b}{c}=2.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector That Is Parallel To a Plane
questions.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨a,\,0,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨-1,1,3⟩=\sqrt{7}.$ What is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨-1,1,3⟩=\sqrt{7}$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-1,1,3⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,1,3⟩ & =0 \\ -{t}_{1}+{t}_{2}+3{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{1} & ={t}_{2}+3{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{2}+3{t}_{3},\,{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{2},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the second component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{2}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{3}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{3}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨3,\,0,\,1⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{a}{c}=3.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Straight Line
questions.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(1,-2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(4,1,-3)$ and $B(7,-3,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨1,-2,3⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(4,1,-3)$ and $B(7,-3,1)$, we can find a vector that is parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨7,-3,1⟩-⟨4,1,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-4,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨3,-4,4⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,4⟩ & =⟨1,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,4⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,4⟩ & =23.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Straight Line
questions.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(-3,2,1)$ and is  perpendicular to the line 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+6t \\ y=3-5t \\ z=-2+4t.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨-3,2,1⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+6t \\ y=3-5t \\ z=-2+4t\end{aligned}\,⇒\,⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨-1,3,-2⟩+t\text{ }{{⟨6,-5,4⟩}_{⏟}}_{v}.
$$

   

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨6,-5,4⟩.$ So, a normal  vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨6,-5,4⟩.
$$

 

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨6,-5,4⟩ & =⟨-3,2,1⟩\cdot ⟨6,-5,4⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨6,-5,4⟩ & =-24.\end{aligned}
$$
